To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

fermentation temperature, thermofiltration, must freezing, pectolyse, saignee and extended maceration are techniques that increase phenolic extraction in red wines, whereas sulfur dioxide, cold maceration and carbonic maceration have variable effects depending on the grape variety studied, and skin and grape juice mixing have no effect on phenolics.
the phenolic composition is a complex issue that depends on many factors and is not easy to predict.
winemaking practices and techniques have been shown to affect the phenolics in wine.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of the winemaking techniques on the phenolic extraction in the wine.
the effects of the winemaking process on the phenolic composition, particularly anthocyanins and tannins, of red wine.
the effect of winemaking techniques and processing variables on the phenolic extraction in red wines.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

no winemaking variable has been shown to have a universal effect on phenolic extraction, and that the effects of each variable are dependent on the grape variety, vintage, and the winemaking techniques used.
the impact of winemaking techniques and parameters on the phenolics of finished red wines remains unclear and that more studies are needed to elucidate this important topic.
no one winemaking technique or practice is universally applicable to all grape varieties.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the winemaker has a significant degree of control over the phenolic profile and composition of red wines.
there are no universal winemaking techniques that increase the phenolic content in red wines.
there is a great need for further research to determine which of these techniques are most effective and to determine the optimal conditions for their use.
The main takeaway from our work is that
winemaking practices can be employed to increase the phenolic concentration of wines.
winemakers can manipulate the phenolic composition by using different processing and fermentation parameters, but the effects are often variety and vintage dependent.
winemakers can influence phenolic composition through their choice of winemaking variables.
